# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication with Blind, since Mute can hear me and see nothing, and Blind can hear neither speech nor see gestures, but can hear speech through... wait, let me reconsider.

Actually: Blind cannot see or touch-related-symbols, but Blind CAN hear speech (only "hear anything" is disallowed for Deaf, not Blind). Let me recheck the table: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so Blind can hear! I need to speak (not gesture) to reach Blind. Gestures only reach Mute (since Mute can see... wait no, Mute cannot see either per the channel rules given: "When you gesture, Mute receives it" - so Mute receives gestures, meaning Mute can see).

So: Deaf speaks -> Mute and Blind both receive (per "your channels" section). Deaf gestures -> only Mute receives.

This is my first turn with an empty board and no prior context. I should report what I see to both Mute and Blind via speech, since Mute has the manual and needs this info, and Blind needs it too but can't read gestures - speech reaches both.

```
speak(text="Display reads zero. Light is yellow. Five wires in order: one white, two green, three yellow, four blue, five red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Let me fix this - I need to only use symbols from the allowed alphabet, and I should only submit one set of calls (not two conflicting attempts).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute gestured [☝ ✌] then [✌ 👍]. Mute can only gesture to me (I can see), and I can only gesture back to Mute. Blind can't see gestures at all. Since Mute cannot speak, and I cannot hear, gestures are our only channel - but they're very limited (just blanks-carrying symbols with no predefined meaning, per the rules "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something").

I already gave Mute all the board info via speech (which Blind also received). Mute is likely trying to confirm something about wire 2 (✌ could mean "2") or acknowledge receipt. Since I can't establish rich meaning through gestures alone without prior agreement, let me try building simple numeric conventions: assume ☝=1, ✌=2, and 👍=yes/confirm, 👎=no.

If Mute gestured [☝ ✌] then [✌ 👍], perhaps they're asking about wire "1" then "2", or confirming wire 2 is correct/important. Let me try to confirm this reading back.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures from Mute this turn — likely Blind spoke (since speaking order is Blind, Mute, Deaf, and Blind's speech reaches Mute and me... wait, actually only Mute and I receive Deaf's speech per my channels, but does Blind's speech reach me?

Let me reconsider the channel table: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it. You never receive speech." So I (Deaf) never receive speech from anyone - consistent with being deaf. So Blind and Mute may be talking to each other via speech, and I only see gestures directed at me from Mute (Mute cannot speak, only gesture — wait Mute "cannot speak" per the role table). So Mute can only gesture to communicate, and only I can see gestures. So Mute's only way to relay information is through me.

Blind can speak (not restricted) and hearing works for both Mute and... does Blind's speech reach Deaf? "You never receive speech" - so no, I never get Blind's speech either.

So the channel is: Blind speaks -> Mute hears (Mute can hear, just can't speak). Mute gestures -> I see. I speak -> Mute and Blind hear. I gesture -> Mute sees.

So Blind and Mute can converge info through me and each other. I already told them both the board via speech. Now empty context suggests nothing new for me. Let me wait, or proactively repeat key info via gesture to Mute in case they need reconfirmation, using simple numeral coding.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫵]

Mute is gesturing [✌ 🫵] - possibly "2" and "you/this one" (pointing gesture, often means "you" or "that one"). This could be Mute confirming or asking about wire 2 specifically, maybe the manual says wire 2 (green) is significant, or asks me to confirm color of wire 2.

Since I already told Mute wire 2 is green, perhaps Mute wants me to double check or emphasize wire 2. Let me confirm wire 2's color specifically since that seems to be the focus.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Wire two is green, in case that matters for what you do next.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new. Blind may have spoken to Mute directly (not visible to me), and Mute may now be relaying info to Blind via... wait, Mute cannot speak at all, so Mute cannot relay to Blind directly! Mute can only gesture, and only I can see gestures. So Mute's only way to get info to Blind is through ME - Mute gestures to me, I interpret, then I speak to Blind.

This means I'm the critical relay from Mute to Blind. I need to actively solicit gestures from Mute about what the manual says regarding this specific bomb configuration (display 0, yellow light, wires: white/green/yellow/blue/red), then translate to Blind.

Let me try establishing a numbering system with Mute for wires 1-5, and ask which wire to cut.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute gestured [✌ 👍] again - this seems to confirm "2" = "yes/correct". Combined with the earlier [✌ 🫵], this strongly suggests wire 2 (green) is the correct wire to cut according to the manual, and Mute is confirming this to me repeatedly.

I should relay this to Blind clearly via speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has confirmed twice now, pointing at wire two. Cut wire two, the green one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb state changed after cutting wire 2 (green, now marked CUT). New state: display still 0, light now blue, wires: 1:yellow, 2:CUT, 3:blue, 4:red, 5:white. This is a new round with new colors, so previous wire-color mapping doesn't apply anymore. I need to relay this fresh information to both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(text="Wire two is cut. New state: display shows zero, light is now blue. Remaining wires: one yellow, two cut, three blue, four red, five white.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

Mute gestured [🖐 👍] - 🖐 could mean "5" (five fingers) and 👍 confirming. This suggests wire 5 (white) is the next correct wire per the manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is pointing at wire five now. Cut wire five, the white one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👍"])
wait()
```
